label: Born
description: Born on 13 November 1924, as indicated by dying on his seventieth birthday in 1994.

sources.quote: Motoo Kimura died on 13 November 1994, his seventieth birthday.

label: Died
description: Died on 13 November 1994, his seventieth birthday.

sources.quote: Motoo Kimura died on 13 November 1994, his seventieth birthday.

label: Began graduate studies at University of Wisconsin
description: Research began with association as a graduate student with James F. Crow and Sewall Wright.

sources.quote: Kimura's research began with his association (as a graduate student) with James F. Crow, and also Sewall Wright, at the University of Wisconsin, in 1954.

label: Formal mathematical work period
description: Period of purely mathematical work in stochastic theory that made his reputation.

sources.quote: The first is his more formal purely mathematical work, which took up much of his time in the period 1954-1968, and which made his reputation

label: Advanced neutral theory of evolution
description: Advanced the neutral, or non-Darwinian, theory of evolution claiming much genetic variation arose from random changes rather than selection.

sources.quote: He thus advanced, in 1968, the neutral, or non-Darwinian, theory of evolution

label: Joined Applied Probability Editorial Board
description: Became a member of the Applied Probability Editorial Board from its creation.

sources.quote: Motoo Kimura was a member of the Applied Probability Editorial Board from its creation in 1964 through to the end of 1969.

label: Left Applied Probability Editorial Board
description: Ended membership on the Applied Probability Editorial Board.

sources.quote: Motoo Kimura was a member of the Applied Probability Editorial Board from its creation in 1964 through to the end of 1969.

label: Autobiographical account published
description: Published 'Diffusion models of population genetics in the age of molecular biology' in The Craft of Probabilistic Modelling.

sources.quote: For an autobiographical account see 'Diffusion models of population genetics in the age of molecular biology', in The Craft of Probabilistic Modelling, ed. 1. Gani, pp. 150-165, Springer-Verlag, Heidelberg, 1986.
